thoughts.content: No prior incidents/memory for this signature — this is a fresh investigation. Let's check the deployment and pods in the shop namespace.
New RS api-57f65dc5db (desired=1) has current=0 — it can't even create pods. Old RS api-f64486c4c still serves 2/2. Let's find out why pod creation is blocked.

Clear mechanism found: ResourceQuota compute-resources in namespace shop enforces requests.memory limit of 200Mi, and current usage is already at 200Mi (exactly at the cap) from the running pods (2x api, 2x frontend, loadgen, redis, worker). The rolling update's surge pod (api-57f65dc5db, maxSurge 25% → needs 1 extra pod requesting 32Mi) is being rejected by the quota admission controller every time, so the new ReplicaSet can never create any pod → rollout permanently stuck (ReplicaFailure: FailedCreate). Let me confirm the quota object itself and check if this is new/recent (what changed).

Root Cause Analysis: KubeDeploymentRolloutStuck — shop/api

Classification: CONFIRMED

What's broken
kubectl describe deployment api -n shop shows:
``
Replicas: 2 desired | 0 updated | 2 total | 2 available | 1 unavailable
Conditions: ReplicaFailure=True (Reason: FailedCreate)
NewReplicaSet: api-57f65dc5db (0/1 replicas created)
`
The new ReplicaSet api-57f65dc5db has been retrying pod creation repeatedly (10+ FailedCreate events, "combined from similar events x5") and has created zero of its desired 1 pod. This matches the alert exactly: rollout genuinely not progressing, not a stale/transient alert.

Mechanism (root cause)
Every pod-creation attempt by the new ReplicaSet is rejected by namespace admission control:
`
Error creating: pods "api-57f65dc5db-*" is forbidden: exceeded quota: compute-resources,
requested: requests.memory=32Mi, used: requests.memory=200Mi, limited: requests.memory=200Mi
`
Confirmed via kubectl get resourcequota compute-resources -n shop -o yaml:
`
hard: requests.memory: 200Mi
used: requests.memory: 200Mi   ← zero headroom
`
And the current steady-state memory requests across all 7 running pods in shop sum to exactly 200Mi (api 32+32, frontend 16+16, loadgen 8, redis 32, worker 64 = 200Mi) — so the namespace quota is pinned at its hard cap with no slack.

The deployment's rollout strategy is RollingUpdate with maxSurge: 25%, maxUnavailable: 25% (kubectl get deployment api -o jsonpath='{.spec.strategy}'). With 2 desired replicas, 25% surge rounds up to 1 extra pod that must exist simultaneously with the 2 old pods during the rollout. That surge pod needs 32Mi of additional quota headroom that does not exist — so admission control rejects it every single time, forever, and the rollout can never progress past 0/1 on the new RS.

Why now
The rollout was triggered by a kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation (a rollout restart, revision 2) at the same timestamp the namespace/quota were created — i.e., the very first rollout attempted agains
